sources.title: Democratizing access to large-scale language models with OPT-175B
sources.evidence: Dated May 3, 2022; explicitly releases smaller baseline models including 125 million parameters, with pretrained weights and a noncommercial research license.

sources.title: OPT: Open Pre-trained Transformer Language Models, Table 1 and Sections 2 and D
sources.evidence: The 125M row specifies 12 layers, 12 attention heads and width 768. The suite uses decoder-only Transformers, ReLU and 2048-token training sequences. Appendix D explicitly applies the noncommercial weight license to the smaller baselines.

sources.title: facebook/opt-125m configuration
sources.evidence: Exact OPTForCausalLM configuration: hidden size and embedding width 768, FFN width 3072, 12 layers, 12 heads, vocabulary 50272, 2048 positions, pre-layer normalization, ReLU and Transformers 4.21.0.dev0.

sources.title: facebook/opt-125m model card
sources.publisher: Hugging Face, hosted in Meta official model repository
sources.evidence: The card identifies this as a pretrained-only causal language model for text generation and downstream fine-tuning. It states a May 3, 2022 original release and explains that Hugging Face authored this card; the original Meta card is in the paper.

sources.title: OPT-125M distributed weight license
sources.evidence: The exact repository distributes the OPT-175B License Agreement. Its grant is solely for non-commercial research and its restrictions exclude commercial or production purposes; this is the weight license, distinct from the code license.

sources.title: Transformers v4.21.0 OPT implementation
sources.evidence: Defines dense attention and two-layer FFNs, parameter embeddings with two additional positional rows, biased attention/FFN linear layers, two affine layer norms per block, the conditional final norm and a bias-free tied language-model head.

sources.title: Transformers v4.21.0 OPT configuration defaults
sources.evidence: The default _remove_final_layer_norm is false. With the exact config do_layer_norm_before=true this includes the final affine layer norm; equal embedding and hidden dimensions introduce no input/output projection matrices.

sources.title: Official OPT pretrained checkpoint listing
sources.evidence: Lists OPT-125M, nominal size 125M and a direct pretrained checkpoint URL. The current link uses v1_20230405, a later package revision that does not replace the original public release date. Weight use is governed by MODEL_LICENSE.md.

sources.title: Hugging Face metadata for facebook/opt-125m
sources.evidence: The official repository resolves to 27dcfa74d334bc871f3234de431e71c6eeba5dd6 and was created May 11, 2022, after the original release. Metadata lists PyTorch, TensorFlow and Flax weight files; no weight file was downloaded.

sources.title: Meta metaseq Transformer decoder reference implementation
sources.evidence: Defines ordinary Transformer blocks and final affine layer norm. Shared embeddings directly assign output_projection.weight to embed_tokens.weight. decoder.version is registered as a buffer, and attention-mask tensors are not learned parameters.

sources.title: Transformers v4.21.0 shared configuration defaults
sources.evidence: tie_word_embeddings defaults to true. The official OPT-125M config does not override it.

sources.title: Transformers v4.21.0 weight tying implementation
sources.evidence: With tie_word_embeddings true and TorchScript false, tie_weights assigns output and input embeddings the same weight Parameter, rather than a second independent learned matrix.

name.note: Catalog display spelling corresponds to the exact official OPT-125M checkpoint.

developer.note: Developed and released by Meta AI; Meta is the catalog developer label.

family.note: The exact configuration declares model_type=opt and the paper identifies the OPT family.

release_date.note: The dated original Meta announcement explicitly releases the 125M baseline. May 11 is the HF hosting creation date; neither that nor the later checkpoint package revision is the original release.

open_weights.note: The exact pretrained model has a direct Meta checkpoint link and publicly listed official HF weights. Availability does not imply an unrestricted license.

license.note: Supported descriptive name for the custom OPT-175B License Agreement distributed with OPT-125M; limited to non-commercial research, independent of the metaseq source-code license.

parameters_b.note: Derived complete unique registered parameter-element count for the official HF configuration, not a checkpoint-header measurement. With H=768, F=3072, L=12, V=50272 and P=2048: V*H + (P+2)*H + L*(4*H*H + 4*H + 2*H*F + F + H + 4*H) + 2*H = 38,608,896 + 1,574,400 + 12*7,087,872 + 1,536 = 125,239,296 = 0.125239296B. The shared embedding/LM-head matrix is counted once; attention and FFN biases, two affine norms per block and the final affine norm are included. Equal embedding/hidden widths require no projection matrices. The positional table includes its two reserved offset/padding rows; this counts full parameter tensors, not a claim that every scalar was updated during training. Version/mask buffers, KV caches and duplicate serialization aliases are excluded. Meta publishes the rounded nominal label 125M. No full weight download or unpickling occurred.

active_parameters_b.note: The sources define the architecture and total parameter tensors but do not define or separately report an active-per-token parameter count. Dense architecture alone is insufficient to substitute the total, especially for indexed embedding tables.

architecture.note: A decoder-only Transformer with 12 standard self-attention/FFN blocks, 12 attention heads, width 768 and FFN width 3072. The exact implementation has no expert routing or sparse MoE modules.

context_window.note: max_position_embeddings=2048 agrees with the paper training sequence length. Two positional offset rows are implementation padding and do not extend the usable context to 2050 tokens.

modalities.note: Text-token inputs and vocabulary-logit text generation; the exact causal-LM model contains no image, audio or video encoders/decoders.

reasoning.note: The exact pretrained base model has no separately documented dedicated reasoning mode or reasoning-training feature. Prompted text reasoning does not establish a native reasoning-mode flag, and absence of documentation does not prove inability.

tool_call.note: No native tool-call schema, protocol or dedicated tool-use training is specified for this base checkpoint. The documented text-generation interface and external wrappers do not establish a native tool-call feature.

description.value: Meta's OPT-125M pretrained dense decoder-only Transformer for text generation.
description.note: Variant-specific description supported by the paper, exact checkpoint card and model implementation.

patch.description: Meta's OPT-125M pretrained dense decoder-only Transformer for text generation.
patch.notes: Published nominal size: 125M. The 125,239,296 total is derived from the official HF configuration and matching reference definitions, counting tied token/output embeddings once, all biases/norms and the full positional table including two reserved rows; it is not checkpoint-header verified. Active parameters are not separately defined or reported. This is a pretrained text model with no documented native reasoning mode or tool-call protocol. Weights use the custom non-commercial research license. Original release: May 3, 2022; HF repository creation: May 11, 2022.

summary: Reconciled the nominal 125M label to 125,239,296 unique configured parameter elements, including tied-weight, positional-offset, bias and normalization accounting. Kept active parameters null rather than assuming dense equals total. Confirmed original May 3, 2022 release, public research weights, custom non-commercial weight license, dense architecture, 2048-token context and text-only modalities. Kept native reasoning/tool flags null because they are not separately documented for this pretrained-only checkpoint and replaced the generic description. No full weights were downloaded; the exact total is derived from config/reference code rather than checkpoint headers.
